items.title: ggml reaches a 1.0 release
items.oneliner: ggml 1.0 adds FP8 and backend speedups, making local inference stacks look more production-grade than hobbyist.

items.title: Qwen3.8 quantization gets materially better
items.oneliner: Unsloth says Dynamic v3.1 lifts Qwen3.8-27B accuracy 5 to 10 percent, which directly changes local deployment tradeoffs.

items.title: Serving giant models now spans boxes
items.oneliner: Nvidia served 753B-parameter GLM-5.3 at 607.8 tok/s across two DGX stations, normalizing multi-node inference engineering.

items.title: Lovable apps leaked sensitive user data
items.oneliner: Researchers found 159,000 Lovable apps exposing passport data and 200,000 private messages, a brutal warning for vibe-coded products.

items.title: Danfoss fridge controllers are actively exploitable
items.oneliner: Danfoss controller bugs caused tens of millions in spoiled food, proving OT security failures now have very physical costs.

items.title: Apache shipped a critical RCE fix
items.oneliner: Apache flagged CVE-2026-119618 as critical in mod_http2, so exposed 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 servers need immediate patching.

items.title: Italy hit Meta with a massive fine
items.oneliner: Italy fined Meta $887 million over Android data access, showing European privacy enforcement still has real financial teeth.

items.title: Non-English prompts cost more energy
items.oneliner: University of Michigan found generative AI uses more energy on non-English text, exposing an overlooked multilingual infrastructure tax.

items.title: A browser built specifically for agents
items.oneliner: Agweb gives coding agents isolated workspaces and a shared dashboard, hinting that agent UX is becoming its own product category.

items.title: Lean found bugs in tax law
items.oneliner: A Lean formalization surfaced 138 drafting mistakes in the US tax code, which is exactly the kind of boring AI win enterprises trust.
